title: POC Pilot: INT8 / FP8 KPI Checkpoint
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing INT8 and FP8 pilot results. Team compared quality regressions vs baseline, perf deltas (p50/p95 latencies), and cost estimates. SE proposed kernel and batching tweaks; customer to run a 10k prompt eval and share error cases. Agreement to test a canary fallback to FP8 when confidence drops. Action items and timing clarified.
transcript:
Header: 2025-09-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins | Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leo (Opsurge), Priya (Opsurge SRE), Angela (Opsurge PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we' re on for fifty minutes today, quick agenda — results, tuning, next steps.
[01:02] Leo: cool, yes thanks. we've been running the INT8 profile across the nightly set, about 5k unique prompts so far, results here are — p50 is down 18% latency, p95 down 12%, cost per token roughly -42% vs fp32. but quality has some bumps, mainly short-form generation hallucinations.
[02:10] Maya: right, we saw those too. the top three failure modes: entity hallucination, broken dates, and truncation in long-context. interestingly FP8 had slightly better held coherence on longer seqs, but INT8 wins on tail latency.
[03:25] Priya: just to be clear on infra — are you running on dedicated nodes or hosted for these runs? network jitter may affect p95.
[03:50] Jordan: these are on dedicated pilot pool, gpus reported as A100-80GB, kernel v2.1.1. Maya you wanna recap kernel changes?
[04:08] Maya: sure — we switched to the int8-perf kernels (there's a new comb-vec path) and enabled continuous batching at 64 where safe. also enabled prefix KV cache (sometimes shows in logs as KV cash) which reduced recompute on repeated contexts.
[05:30] Carlos: note that the batching bump is workload dependent — for your interactive workloads, throughput is up but tail latency can spike when batch aggregation waits. so we tuned max-agg-wait to 8ms.
[07:00] Angela: from product side we care about quality thresholds: less than 1.5% increase in hallucinations vs baseline or we can't move to INT8 for customer-facing features. what are we seeing today?
[07:35] Leo: currently at ~2.8% increase on the production prompt set. but if we drop certain prompt templates (the date-heavy ones) it goes to ~1.2%.
[08:10] Maya: that suggests prompt-specific sensitivity. i propose two levers: selective quantization by route (serve FP8 for those templates) or contextual fallback — detect low-confidence tokens and fall back to FP8/FP16 for that request.
[09:05] Jordan: could we do a canary that auto-falls back on confidence score < 0.7?
[09:20] Maya: yes, we built that prototype — it adds ~8% cost on the affected requests but keeps overall cost savings. it also requires a small change to your routing rules.
[11:00] Leo: what's the perf hit on fallback? if we fallback to FP8 mid-request, does that refill KV cache?
[11:25] Maya: good q. when we fallback mid-request we flush the kv and recompile path — so you take a penalty on that request, avg +120ms. if you fallback whole-request (route to FP8) no kv flush. so recommendation is route-level fallback.
[13:00] Priya: are there memory/regression risks with FP8? we saw some bit-flip concerns historically but that might be overblown.
[13:20] Carlos: FP8 in our runtime uses a simulated 8-bit mantissa with clipped dynamic ranges; we add quant-stability checks. we haven't seen memory corruption in the pilot.
[15:00] Angela: can we walk through an example error case?
[15:30] Leo: yes — sample prompt id 4,237: asks for timeline of events, INT8 introduced 'June 2024' where baseline had 'July 2024' — subtle but customer-visible.
[16:10] Maya: that looks like calibration shift — our scale factors need per-layer refinement. quick fix is per-layer recalibration with the 1k representative corpus. takes about 2 hours to run.
[17:50] Jordan: okay thanks. let's talk metrics: can you confirm p50/p95 numbers?
[18:10] Leo: p50: 22ms -> down to 18ms on INT8; p95: 120ms -> 105ms. throughput up ~1.9x. tokens/sec measured under sustained load was 2.1k -> 4.0k.
[20:00] Maya: those throughput numbers align. on cost we estimate a 38-46% reduction on per-token infra spend for INT8 vs fp32, FP8 is around 30-35% reduction but with better quality in long contexts.
[21:30] Priya: customer-facing SLAs require p95 < 150ms so we're good there.
[22:10] Angela: the product asks for an A/B where 10% of traffic goes to INT8 and we monitor NPS/EDU metrics — is that doable?
[22:50] Jordan: yes, Redwood routing supports percent rollouts and automatic fallback policies. we'll provide a rollout config.
[24:30] Leo: quick ask — can you share the per-token latency CSV and the raw eval diffs? the earlier sheet had some missing rows.
[24:55] Maya: i'll post updated CSV today, includes per-route breakdown and kernel tags. expect a link in the recap.
[26:00] Carlos: also include the kernel hash and compilation flags — that helps reproduce.
[27:30] Leo: on the evaluation side, we're seeing that certain prompt family "customer-attr" spikes errors — do we have an inline scorer to apply family-specific thresholds?
[28:05] Maya: yes, we can add per-route quality budgets and tie alerts to those budgets. that way if family A hits >1.5% hallucinations we pause the route.
[30:00] Angela: what's the plan to reduce the 2.8% delta down to <1.5%?
[30:20] Maya: three parallel actions: 1) per-layer recalibration on the int8 quant tables, 2) selective route exclusion for sensitive templates, 3) small augmentation to the training calibration set with 2k edge-cases to reduce scale drift.
[32:00] Leo: how long do these take?
[32:10] Maya: recalibration 2–3 hours, route config change is immediate, augmentation and re-eval about 48 hours.
[33:40] Jordan: okay for timelines, can we agree to a week cadence? next check in to validate the 10k eval run.
[34:05] Leo: yes we'll run the 10k and flag top 50 regressions.
[35:30] Priya: one operational note — our SRE needs an audit log of model invocations for compliance. does Redwood provide per-request traces?
[36:00] Carlos: yes, request-level tracing exists in Console with 30d retention on this pilot. we can export logs to your S3 via our webhook.
[37:10] Angela: and encryption? key management?
[37:30] Jordan: we support KMS and customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated; pilot used Redwood-managed keys but we can shift to your key for Dedicated pilot.
[39:00] Leo: competitor checks — we briefly eval'd Anthropic's endpoints, Cohere — they had similar latency but higher cost in our run. nothing disqualifying but worth noting.
[40:10] Maya: also called out that some open model variants have different tokenization which affected the prompt results.
[41:20] Jordan: next steps recap — run 10k eval, Maya shares CSV & kernel hash, Jordan sends updated pilot pricing and rollout config, Leo to produce top-50 regressions.
[42:00] Angela: schedule wise, when can we see the recalibration?
[42:15] Maya: i'll kick it tonight and should have preliminary results by Monday 2025-09-15 end of day.
[44:00] Leo: we'll also instrument additional monitoring to capture confidence scores per token.
[44:30] Jordan: on the canary fallback — we'll provide a config that routes to FP8 when confidence < 0.7 and also a full-route exclusion flag for known-sensitive templates.
[46:00] Priya: any risks if we flip 10% traffic? can we throttle ramp?
[46:20] Carlos: yes ramping is recommended: 1% -> 5% -> 10% with 24–48 hours between steps, automatic rollback on quality budget breach.
[48:00] Angela: ok good. soooo last items — pricing ask, high level SLA, and export of logs.
[48:30] Jordan: i'll share a short proposal today. SLA for Dedicated pilot is draft 99.9% with p95 targets — we'll include in the document.
[49:10] Leo: thanks all, we'll have the 10k run by Thursday and post results in the shared sheet.
[50:00] Jordan: great — thanks everyone, we'll reconvene next Monday same time.
[51:20] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript has minor auto-caption errors (e.g., "KV cash"), speaker overlap present.
